text: In the laser-neuron rate equations, excitability arises from a separation of timescales. Which identification is correct?
choices: The carrier density is the fast variable (photon lifetime) and the optical field is the slow variable (carrier lifetime)
The optical field is the fast variable (photon lifetime ~ps) and the carrier density is the slow recovery variable (carrier lifetime ~ns)
Both field and carriers evolve on the same picosecond timescale
The refractory period is set by the fast photon lifetime
explanation: The book gives the photon lifetime tau_p ~ ps as the fast timescale (optical field) and the carrier lifetime tau_s ~ ns as the slow recovery timescale (carrier density), with ratio tau_s/tau_p ~ 10^2-10^3. Choice 0 swaps the roles; choice 2 denies the required separation; and the refractory recovery is set by the slow carrier lifetime, not the fast photon lifetime, so choice 3 is wrong.
